summary: The comparative reporting layer generally retains short, wide, thin, low-ratio, tortuous, and single-slice tracks as morphology warnings, uses technical-valid tracks as the primary population, avoids WT-specific tracking objectives, and labels ROI exposure as sampled rather than anatomical organ volume. However, the production U-Net-primary path converts measured length above 20 um directly into suspected_multi_object_merge and then a technical failure. Length alone does not establish fusion, so plausible unusually long mutant morphology can be excluded from the primary population. The claim that technical-valid detections remain measurable across plausible variation and that morphology warnings never become comparative technical vetoes therefore fails.

findings.title: Length above 20 um is an automatic comparative technical veto
findings.impact: A genuine unusually long mutant nucleus can be removed from the primary technical-valid population solely because of its morphology. This can erase or attenuate the phenotype being studied and contradicts the claim that morphology warnings do not become comparative acceptance rules.
evidence: sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3424-3431 defines the above-20-um review band solely from measured length.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:3461-3462 sets suspected_multi_object_merge to geodesic_um > 20.0 without requiring topology, multiple seeds, manual masks, or other fusion evidence.
sperm_segmentation_saturnv5.7.1.py:6820-6823 treats suspected_multi_object_merge as clear_multi_object_connected_component technical failure.
tests/test_saturn_v57_unet_primary.py:374-403 confirms that this length-only classification makes the track technical-invalid.
production_profiles/saturn_v5_7_1_model_c_epoch003.json:29, :74-77, and :193 show that U-Net-primary production uses overlong splitting and a 20-um reconstructed-length guard.
findings.recommendation: Keep length above 20 um as a morphology/manual-review annotation unless independent technical evidence establishes fusion. Define technical fusion using evidence such as multiple confident cores/seeds, branch topology, discontinuous masks, implausible cross-Z joining, or reviewed manual masks. Preserve the unsplit source measurement and add synthetic tests proving that both a genuine long single object and a true fused component receive appropriate, distinct dispositions.

findings.title: Production-candidate evidence does not biologically classify the substantial below-2-um population
findings.impact: Counts and specimen summaries include hundreds of very short tracks whose mixture of genuine nuclei, partials, split fragments, missed joins, and noise is unknown. Although retaining them is preferable to phenotype-directed deletion, production count validity and sensitivity remain unresolved.
evidence: V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:86-90 reports 831 KJ-01 and 560 WT-01 tracks below 2 um and says many are single-plane U-Net fragments.
audits/claims_registry.json:127-153 defines a separate claim requiring blinded stratified classification and explicitly states that length below 2 um is not automatically noise.
V5_7_1_VALIDATION_REPORT.md:101-104 calls the pipeline ready for a controlled full-study run while acknowledging that the below-2-um sensitivity stratum still requires classification.
findings.recommendation: Before interpreting production counts or group differences, perform blinded stratified review using raw images, probability maps, instance masks, and adjacent-Z context across independent WT and mutant specimens. Report the primary preserved population plus sensitivity analyses based only on technically justified classifications.

findings.title: Adversarial biological coverage is incomplete for thin and fragmented-looking primary instances
findings.impact: Source inspection does not establish that all required plausible morphology classes survive segmentation, tracking, and reporting under the frozen production profile.
evidence: tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:840-868 covers short, long, wide, tortuous, and single-slice track auditing.
tests/test_saturn_v57_multisample.py:298-338 covers low-ratio rescue.

No focused named test found in the inspected evidence demonstrates an intentionally thin or fragmented-looking U-Net-primary instance surviving the complete production path without phenotype-directed loss.
findings.recommendation: Add calibrated synthetic/adversarial cases for thin continuous masks, curved masks, fragmented-looking but biologically continuous masks, true fusions, and long single objects. Assert source-detection preservation, warning versus failure disposition, tracking behavior, and inclusion in primary reports.

limitations: No full image stack was run, as required.
Focused pytest execution was blocked by the read-only environment because Python could not create a temporary file; conclusions rely on source, configuration, report, and test-assertion inspection.
No other reviewers' outputs were read.
Manual image masks, raw pilot images, and external biological validation were not available in the inspected claim evidence.

The working tree is pre-commit and dirty; git status showed modified and untracked files, although HEAD matched d8c498ca3c76b17ce76c02dc85bed5d9ac542d0b. Conclusions apply to the inspected working-tree implementation, not solely to immutable commit contents.
recommended_follow_up: Remove the length-only technical-failure rule or supplement it with independent technical fusion evidence, then rerun biological-validity review.
Conduct blinded classified review of the below-2-um stratum across independent WT and mutant specimens before count-based biological inference.
Add end-to-end adversarial tests for thin, curved, fragmented-looking, fused-looking, long-single-object, and single-slice cases under the exact frozen production profile.
Rerun focused tests in a writable temporary environment and attach the reproducible command output to the superseding audit run.
Require manual masks or external biological validation before asserting fusion, true nuclear anatomy, segmentation sensitivity, or a biological WT-versus-mutant effect.
